2) We have some questions specific to tokenization: our corpus is mixed English/Spanish, and some user-generated content in short chat-like fragments. Can you provide guidance on expected tokenization deltas across model families and any recommended packaging (e.g., committed token blocks vs pay-as-you-go) that helps smooth this variability?

As background: our current POC averages ~12M raw characters/day (~1M words/day), so monthly usage could be 20M–60M tokens depending on model. We need a quick cost projection to include in next week's procurement packet.

Subject: Re: Quick rate card + tokenization question — tokenization delta details

Hi Marta (and team),

I ran an initial pass on a 50k-sample subset of the corpus you provided (mixed EN/ES, user chat snippets, some short-form docs). Summary of what we observed and how it affects billing:

Summary numbers (approx):
- Example document: ~1,000 English words (raw) =>
  - BPE-style tokenizer (model family A): ~1,300 tokens
  - SentencePiece-style tokenizer (model family B): ~1,170 tokens (~10% fewer)
- Spanish segments tended to compress slightly better with SentencePiece in our sample (~8–12% fewer tokens vs the BPE baseline for the same UTF-8 length).
- Short chat fragments (lots of punctuation/emojis) increased tokenization variability; on a per-message basis variance can spike to ~20% but averages out at corpus scale.

Cost impact (using hosted baseline pricing for illustration):
- Hosted baseline: $0.10 per 1k tokens (i.e., $0.0001 per token).
- If model A (BPE) yields 1,300 tokens for a document vs 1,170 tokens for model B (SentencePiece), the delta per doc is 130 tokens = $0.013 per document at baseline.
- Scaling: on 10M generated tokens/month, a 10% tokenization overhead is ~1M extra tokens => $100 at baseline; on 50M tokens/month the difference is ~$500.

Packaging and negotiation suggestions:
- For customers with mixed-model testing, we recommend a 2-step approach:
  1) Short tokenization audit (48–72 hours): we run your representative sample against 2–3 model variants and return a CSV with per-file token counts (we can sign an NDA if needed). Output: token-sample-report.csv (attached).
  2) Based on audit, pick either: pay-as-you-go with a 3–5% buffer in projections; or commit to a monthly token block with a blended rate and a token true-up/reconciliation quarterly.
- Standard discount tiers (hosted API):
  - 0–5M tokens/mo: 0% discount
  - 5–25M tokens/mo: 8% discount
  - 25–100M tokens/mo: 15% discount
  - >100M tokens/mo: 20%+ (custom)
- For procurement speed, a 12-month committed spend with a quarterly reconciliation gives both parties predictability; we can offer a one-time onboarding credit for migration/testing.

Operational notes:
- Token counts depend on tokenizer implementation details (pre-token normalization, Unicode handling) and model vocabulary. SentencePiece models that use byte-level splits can reduce tokens for languages with compound words or diacritics; BPE can be more efficient for some English contractions. The delta isn't purely 'better or worse' — it depends on your text mix and the model architecture.

I attached the token-sample-report.csv and a short intake deck that outlines the audit flow. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to walk through the CSV if useful.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
